message.content: {"passages":[{"reference":"2.29","text":"But when he heard this, he laughed. When we said, “Why are you laughing at us when we are advising you about what is to your advantage?” he replied, “I am laughing at your foolish supposition, because you believe that the human soul is immortal.” And I said, “We are not surprised, Simon, that you are trying to deceive us, but we are astonished at the reasoning by which you deceive even yourself. Tell me, Simon: even if no one else has been fully assured that the soul is immortal, at least you and we have—you because you separated it from a human body, conversed with it, and commanded it; and we because we were there with you, heard the command, and clearly witnessed what it was commanded to do.” Simon said, “I know what you are saying, but you do not know what matters you are discussing.” Nicetas said, “Since you know, tell us. But if you do not know, do not imagine that you can deceive us by saying that you know while we do not. We are not so childish that you can plant in us the cunning suspicion that you know something of the secret matters, and then take us into your power and keep us there while we are tormented by desire.”","lexical_decisions":[{"source_quote":"Γελῶ ὑμῶν τὴν μωρὰν ὑπόληψιν, ὅτι πιστεύετε ἀθάνατον εἶναι τὴν τοῦ ἀνθρώπου ψυχήν.","chosen":"I am laughing at your foolish supposition, because you believe that the human soul is immortal.","rationale":"ὅτι is taken causally, so Simon ridicules their supposition on account of their belief in the soul’s immortality. Taking it as introducing the content of ὑπόληψιν would awkwardly make their believing, rather than the soul’s immortality, the content of the supposition."},{"source_quote":"πεπληροφόρηται","chosen":"has been fully assured","rationale":"The perfect passive expresses settled assurance, not merely having heard or believed a claim."},{"source_quote":"τὸ κελευσθὲν ἐναργῶς ἱστορήσαντες","chosen":"clearly witnessed what it was commanded to do","rationale":"ἱστορέω can mean ascertain, observe, or report; their stated presence favors direct witnessing of the commanded event."},{"source_quote":"τῶν ἀπορρήτων","chosen":"the secret matters","rationale":"The expression denotes things withheld or not to be disclosed; alternatives include “hidden things” and “mysteries.”"},{"source_quote":"ὑποχειρίους λαβὼν ἔχῃς","chosen":"take us into your power and keep us there","rationale":"ὑποχείριος literally describes someone under another’s hand and hence under that person’s control."}],"source_issues":[{"source_quote":"ὅτι πιστεύετε ἀθάνατον εἶναι τὴν τοῦ ἀνθρώπου ψυχήν","issue":"ὅτι can be read causally, as in the translation, or as introducing an explanation or the content of the preceding expression. The causal reading avoids representing Simon as ridiculing a second-order supposition that the others believe something, while preserving πιστεύετε as the verb governing the claim that the soul is immortal.","proposed_reading":"","blocks_publication":false}]},{"reference":"2.30","text":"Simon said, “I know that you know I separated a soul from a human body. But I also know that you do not know this: it is not the dead person’s soul that renders service—since it does not exist—but some demon that acts while itself pretending to be a soul.” Nicetas said, “We have heard many unbelievable things in this life, but we did not expect to hear any statement more senseless than this one. For if a demon pretends to be the dead person’s soul, what need is there for the soul to be separated from the body? Were we not ourselves there and did we not hear you adjuring the soul of the corpse? How, moreover, when one is adjured, does another that was not adjured obey as though frightened? And when you yourself were once questioned by us as to why the spirit-attendances sometimes cease, did you not say, ‘Once a soul has completed the time above ground that it was destined to spend in a body, it goes to Hades’? Did you not also add that the souls of those who died a natural death, because they went there into Hades and are kept under guard, are not readily permitted to come?”","lexical_decisions":[{"source_quote":"ὑπουργεῖ","chosen":"renders service","rationale":"The verb describes acting in a subordinate or assisting capacity without specifying whom the being serves."},{"source_quote":"τοῦ σκήνους τὴν ψυχὴν","chosen":"the soul of the corpse","rationale":"σκῆνος literally means a tent or bodily dwelling; in this necromantic setting it refers to the dead body."},{"source_quote":"αἱ παρεδρίαι","chosen":"the spirit-attendances","rationale":"The plural denotes magical attendance or assistance associated with an attending spirit; possible contextual renderings include “spirit manifestations,” “séances,” or “familiar-spirit services.”"},{"source_quote":"ἰδίῳ θανάτῳ τελευτησάντων","chosen":"those who died a natural death","rationale":"Literally “those who ended by their own/proper death”; the context contrasts completing one’s allotted embodied lifetime with dying prematurely."},{"source_quote":"αὐτόθι εἰς ᾅδην χωρήσασαι","chosen":"because they went there into Hades","rationale":"αὐτόθι is locative, “there/on that spot”; it does not itself mean “immediately.”"}],"source_issues":[{"source_quote":"αἱ παρεδρίαι","issue":"The exact English value of this technical magical plural is uncertain. It can denote attendances or services of assisting spirits and, by extension, their manifestations or sessions. “Spirit-attendances” preserves the underlying attendance terminology without selecting one narrower reconstruction of the practice.","proposed_reading":"","blocks_publication":false}]},{"reference":"2.31","text":"After Nicetas said this, Aquila himself spoke again: “I wanted to learn just this from you, Simon: whether what is adjured is a soul or a demon, what does it fear, so that it does not disregard the oaths?” Simon said, “For it knows that it will suffer punishment if it disobeys.” Aquila said, “Accordingly, if a soul comes when adjured, judgment also takes place. If, then, souls prove to be immortal and judgment certainly takes place, so that even those adjured to an evil deed would be condemned for disobeying, how have you not been afraid to compel them, when those being compelled are punished for disobedience? The fact that you have not yet suffered for what you did is no wonder, since judgment has not yet taken place—the judgment in which you are to pay the penalty for those you compelled, while the one compelled is to come under pardon as having given priority to the oath over the evil deed.” When he heard this, he became angry and threatened us with death unless we kept silent about the things he was doing.","lexical_decisions":[{"source_quote":"τοὺς ὅρκους","chosen":"the oaths","rationale":"In this magical context the oaths function as binding adjurations; “the adjurations” is a viable contextual alternative."},{"source_quote":"Κόλασιν γὰρ παρακούσασα οἶδεν μέλλειν παθεῖν","chosen":"For it knows that it will suffer punishment if it disobeys","rationale":"The aorist participle expresses disobedience preceding the threatened punishment and is naturally represented as a condition in English."},{"source_quote":"εἰ οὖν αἱ ψυχαὶ ἀθάνατοι γίνονται καὶ κρίσις πάντως γίνεται","chosen":"If, then, souls prove to be immortal and judgment certainly takes place","rationale":"The translation treats immortality and judgment as the joined conditions leading to the subsequent question and explicitly represents καὶ as “and.” An apodotic reading, “then judgment also certainly takes place,” is grammatically possible but less consistent with the printed clause sequence and punctuation."},{"source_quote":"αἱ ψυχαὶ ἀθάνατοι γίνονται","chosen":"souls prove to be immortal","rationale":"Literally the souls “become immortal,” but in the argument γίνονται can present immortality as the conclusion demonstrated by their continued activity; “become immortal” remains a possible more literal rendering."},{"source_quote":"περὶ ὧν ἠνάγκασας","chosen":"for those you compelled","rationale":"The relative may refer to the beings Simon compelled. It could alternatively be understood as an elliptical reference to what he compelled them to do."},{"source_quote":"τῆς κακῆς πράξεως τὸν ὅρκον προτιμήσαν","chosen":"having given priority to the oath over the evil deed","rationale":"The rendering preserves the explicit comparison between the binding oath and the evil act without supplying an unstated object such as avoiding or performing the act."}],"source_issues":[{"source_quote":"εἰ οὖν αἱ ψυχαὶ ἀθάνατοι γίνονται καὶ κρίσις πάντως γίνεται, ὥστ’ ἂν καὶ τοὺς ἐπὶ κακῇ πράξει ὁρκισθέντας καταδικασθῆναι παρακούσαντας: πῶς οὐ πεφόβησαι σὺ ἀναγκάζειν, τῶν ἀναγκαζομένων ἐπὶ παρακοῇ κολαζομένων;","issue":"The scope of καὶ κρίσις πάντως γίνεται is syntactically open. The translation joins immortality and judgment as a compound condition leading to the πῶς question, in keeping with the printed colon after παρακούσαντας. Alternatively, καὶ may be apodotic: “If souls prove to be immortal, then judgment also certainly takes place,” followed by the question. No alteration of the supplied Greek is required.","proposed_reading":"","blocks_publication":false},{"source_quote":"περὶ ὧν ἠνάγκασας","issue":"The gender and referent of ὧν are not explicit in context. It may mean “for those whom you compelled” or, with an elliptical complement, “for what you compelled them to do.” The main rendering follows the personal referent continued by τὸ ἀναγκασθέν.","proposed_reading":"","blocks_publication":false},{"source_quote":"τὸ δὲ ἀναγκασθὲν ὑπὸ συγγνώμην γένηται ὡς τῆς κακῆς πράξεως τὸν ὅρκον προτιμήσαν","issue":"The compressed comparison does not explicitly state whether prioritizing the oath caused compliance with the evil deed or amounted to preferring the oath instead of the deed. The translation preserves the comparison rather than supplying either unstated relationship.","proposed_reading":"","blocks_publication":false}]},{"reference":"2.32","text":"After Aquila said these things, I, Clement, asked what, then, were the wonders he performed. They told me, “He makes statues walk; when he rolls onto fire, he is not burned; sometimes he even flies; he makes loaves out of stones; he becomes a snake; he is transformed into a goat; he becomes double-faced; he turns into gold; he opens closed doors; he dissolves iron; at dinners he presents images in forms of every kind; and he causes the utensils in a house to be seen being carried for service as though on their own, while those carrying them are not seen.” As I listened to them saying these things, I was amazed. They also testified that they themselves had been present and had witnessed many such things.","lexical_decisions":[{"source_quote":"Ἀνδριάντας","chosen":"statues","rationale":"The noun denotes statues or sculpted human figures."},{"source_quote":"διπρόσωπος γίνεται","chosen":"he becomes double-faced","rationale":"The compound literally indicates having two faces; “double-faced” preserves the physical marvel here rather than the modern figurative sense of deceitfulness."},{"source_quote":"σίδηρον λύει","chosen":"he dissolves iron","rationale":"λύω can mean loosen, release, undo, or dissolve. With generic “iron,” dissolving or breaking it apart best fits the list of physical marvels, though “loosens iron” remains possible."},{"source_quote":"εἴδωλα παντοδαπῶν ἰδεῶν","chosen":"images in forms of every kind","rationale":"εἴδωλα can denote images, apparitions, or phantasms; the following phrase emphasizes their varied visible forms."},{"source_quote":"ὡς αὐτόματα φερόμενα πρὸς ὑπηρεσίαν","chosen":"being carried for service as though on their own","rationale":"The objects appear self-moving, although the following clause indicates that unseen bearers actually carry them."},{"source_quote":"αὐτοὶ παρόντες ἱστορηκέναι","chosen":"they themselves had been present and had witnessed","rationale":"Their personal presence supports the observational sense of ἱστορέω rather than merely reporting information received from others."}],"source_issues":[]}]}
